notes: Customer summary: EU-headquartered KM vendor for regulated professional services; heavy legal & compliance corpus in multiple languages.
Primary ask: reliable cross-lingual doc search with consistent recall across languages, and material per-query cost reduction vs current stack.
"Need consistent recall across FR/DE/JA — can't have big variance" — quote from Head of Search (Mathilde Roux).
Technical constraints: EU data residency mandatory for corpora classified as legal; must support SSO/SAML + KMS key control; audit logs required for all retrieval events.
Retrieval targets: candidate recall @k=50 >= 0.95 for EN/FR/DE; acceptable degradation up to 0.9 for low-resource languages but business wants roadmap to parity.
Reranker notes: currently using full cross-encoder per-query causing high CPU cost. Interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations (distill, quantize reranker, candidate-size tuning).
Indexing notes: plan to store per-language embeddings and test combined index vs shard-per-language. Concern: memory footprint and HNSW graph rebuilding for frequent updates.
Fallback strategy: automatic translation fallback for queries in low-resource locales; evaluate impact on precision vs native cross-lingual embeddings.
Operational asks: metrics required - per-language recall/precision, per-language latency P95, cost per 1k queries by route, cold-cache vs warm-cache profiles.
Procurement/security blockers: legal needs EU-only contract language + SOC2/ISO proof; security team flagged ISO27001 requirement (open item).
Next POC milestone: Redwood to run 10M doc benchmark, produce per-language PR curves and a cost/latency model for Dedicated reserved capacity (3 scenarios).
Longer-term win criteria: equalized recall across priority languages, sub-150ms rerank end-to-end, 30-50% unit-cost reduction.
